deviation: The draft says Statements of Work "may" document deliverables, so services can be provided under the Agreement alone rather than only under signed SOWs, which breaks the playbook rule. It also drops the "reasonable skill and care" standard for "professional and workmanlike", and makes the Agreement override the SOW by default. On the plus side, the 99.99% availability commitment and 12-hour Security Incident notice favour Arcadia.
suggested_text: 2.1 Provision of Services. The Supplier shall provide the services described in each Statement of Work signed by both parties under this Agreement with reasonable skill and care, using suitably qualified personnel. No services shall be procured or payable except under a signed Statement of Work or Work Order. 2.2 Statements of Work. Each Statement of Work is governed by this Agreement. If there is a conflict, this Agreement prevails unless the Statement of Work expressly identifies the provision of this Agreement it overrides and is signed by authorised representatives of both parties. 2.3 Service Levels. [Retain draft Sections 2.3 to 2.5 as drafted.]
